criteria.reasoning: The memo states "We cannot move the Ruiz fund into general operations" and grounds this in the gift agreement, policy §4.1 and §3.2, and counsel's advice. Nowhere does it suggest the board may do so on October 21 or on its own authority.
The Ruiz section never mentions Ellen M. Ruiz's written consent under UPMIFA § 6(a) as a way to release or modify the restriction. The donor-consent route is omitted entirely.

The memo discusses § 6(d) only for the Calloway fund. It never says § 6(d) is unavailable for the Ruiz fund, and never cites the Ruiz fund's $512,860 value or 2017 establishment against the § 6(d) thresholds, as the PASS text requires.

The memo says the ADN restriction "remains possible and practicable" and that "an operating deficit does not, by itself, make a fund's purpose impossible or impracticable under UPMIFA." But it never mentions a court modification under § 6(c), its requirements or the Attorney General notice. The PASS text requires explaining that court route, so the criterion is not met.

The memo says "nor can we use its earnings or annual distributions to cover operations". It adds that the agreement "limits the use of distributions and investment returns to scholarships for students enrolled in the Associate Degree in Nursing (ADN) program."

The memo never states the Ruiz fund's FY2027 spending-policy distribution of $19,767.33, or any distribution figure; it gives only the $512,860 August 31 value. The criterion fails a memo that omits the distribution.
The memo does not invoke the Ruiz agreement's Section 5 change-in-circumstances clause at all. It notes that the ADN program "is active and currently has 84 enrolled students."

On Joan's loan the memo says "We cannot do this." It quotes Section 4.2: assets "may not be lent to, borrowed by, pledged for, or used to secure the Foundation's operating needs ... whatever the term or rate of the loan."

The memo concludes the Calloway fund "qualifies for administrative modification under UPMIFA § 6(d)". It gives all three reasons: "balance of $18,420 (less than $25,000)", "established in May 1994 (more than 20 years ago)", and the restriction is "impossible to achieve" because the certificate "was closed in 2011".

The memo says AG notice is required 60 days before release. It states "If counsel sends the notice on Monday, October 5, 2026 ... the 60-day notice period will expire on Friday, December 4, 2026. After that date, the Board of Directors may officially approve the modification."

The memo says "we must redirect the fund to a similar purpose—such as the active Office Administration (A.A.S.) program". It adds that "Modifying the restriction into a general operating fund would not be consistent with her expressed charitable intent."

The memo identifies the "Operating Reserve" ($240,000) as "a board-designated (unrestricted) fund" usable "by a majority vote of the full Board". It says "no donor consent or Attorney General notice is required", and proposes releasing $180,000 at the October 21 meeting.

Every value, rule and date traces to the files: $512,860, 84 ADN students, § 6(d)'s $25,000 / 20-year / 60-day terms, Mrs. Calloway's 2002 death with no successor, the October 5 notice date and the $240,000 reserve. December 4, 2026 follows arithmetically. No unsourced threshold, person or approval appears.
